chapter: Southern Illinois roadhouse and St. Louis
title: Playing off and on with Charlie Creath in St. Louis
summary: Joe says he played with Creath only matinees and a few nights; Creath's band was top in St. Louis but he was often absent and had a theme to greet him.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: In other words, you stayed up there for a while, and then you came back to St. Louis...? I wanted to get into that...
No, I never did come back to St. Louis. In and around St. Louis, we played in and out of St. Louis for about four or five weeks, the little towns around St. Louis.
Oh, you never lived in St. Louis.
Oh, no. Not really.
Somehow I got the feeling that you lived there and played Charlie Creath.
Well, I played with Charlie, although I still played with the medicine show.
Well, let me ask you a little bit about Charlie Creath and all that kind of business in St. Louis. Was Charlie the number-one band in St. Louis?
He was just about. He had a...he had something like maybe... It was an eight- or nine-piece band.
Darensbourg - 103
But like I said, I can't remember any of the guys that was in that band.
Well, let me see if I can remember any of the guys that was on his records, and you tell me if they were in his band. I think Burroughs Lovingood was playing piano. Zutty...
Well, naturally I know Zutty.
Was he with Charlie Creath's band when you were around?
No, no, he wasn't with the band.
I think those records were made in 1924. Who else is on those darn records. Willie Humphrey was either playing tenor on some of them or some of those Dewey Jackson records. I'm not sure which.
Well, it wasn't Willie for sure. As a matter of fact, I never did play in his big band regular. When I played with him, it was a matinee deal. You see, once in a while I played with him at night.
And how did their music differ...

The thing I remember about Charlie really was he never was there; half of the time he never was there. But when I was in the band, every time maybe he'd walk in the place, you had to stop playing, and play, [CLAPS], "Clap hands, here comes Charlie..." Guys'd say, "Hey, Charlie's
Darensbourg - 104
in the house; we've got to play that theme."
Did he have another trumpet player that would cover for him, or what?
Yeah, he had another guy playing trumpet.
Where was Dewey Jackson at this time?
I can't remember.
Wasn't he in St. Louis around the same time?
He could have been very well.

Because I think Dewey Jackson recorded in St. Louis, and I'm pretty sure Charlie... Let's see, Charlie recorded "Grandpa's Spells" "Market Street Stomp" and what's the others... Oh, I can't think of the other two. There were four numbers. And Dewey Jackson recorded around that same time, and he was out of St. Louis.
I never knew him then.
Was Charlie from St. Louis?
I think he was.
Well, his sister was.
